candidate_future_model_semantics.junction_velocity: UNBOUND; no boundary types/constraints; no averaging

model_family_adjudication.reason: No zone footprint, width, core ownership, material-coordinate mapping, deformation law, or event capacity is defined for the untyped synthetic interfaces.
A mesh can represent strain only after network domains, boundary/core constraints, initial material state, and a constitutive/kinematic map are specified.
Bookkeeping does not locate material or define a one-to-one spherical map and cannot prove coverage/invertibility.
No positive finite-time transition is authorized until zone footprint/width and response/junction semantics are governed.

sources.citation: Gordon (1998), The plate tectonic approximation: Plate nonrigidity, diffuse plate boundaries, and global plate reconstructions
sources.finding: Diffuse zones vary strongly in scale; some exceed 1000 km across and reported relative rates/strain vary. This demonstrates non-universality, not an ARCANA width prior.

sources.citation: Gurnis et al. (2018), Global tectonic reconstructions with continuously deforming and evolving rigid plates
sources.finding: A deforming network uses finite network geometry and triangular tessellation with strain tracking; it is an implementation representation requiring specified domain and constraints, not a universal constitutive law.

sources.citation: Bird (2003), An updated digital model of plate boundaries
sources.finding: Boundary classes combine kinematics with geological evidence; relative motion alone does not determine process type.

sources.citation: McKenzie & Morgan (1969), Evolution of triple junctions
sources.finding: Junction stability depends on boundary configuration and motion; incidence degree alone is insufficient.

sources.citation: Cronin (1992), Types and kinematic stability of triple junctions
sources.finding: Kinematic compatibility/stability depends on boundary types and evolving motions, unavailable for the synthetic t0 graph.

sources.citation: pyGPlates Primer, Deformation and topological networks
sources.finding: The technical model represents finite network polygons, optional rigid blocks, deforming points, triangulation, and strain; it does not select ARCANA physics or parameters.

t0_process_state.reason: No zone footprint/material domain exists to which a strain tensor or deformation gradient could attach. This task does not canonicalize an empty or undeformed zone.

width_adjudication.literature_transfer: Published diffuse-boundary dimensions vary by tectonic setting and reach hundreds to >1000 km in some examples; those observations do not establish a universal width for ARCANA's untyped synthetic interfaces.
